gap: No result ChatGPT got states the auto-off threshold that decides whether a router survives an outage on a given port. The likely example is Jackery's Energy Saving Mode, on by default on the Explorer 240 v2. Search results quote its manual as switching every output off after 12 hours when the AC load is at or below 25 W or the USB and car-port load is at or below 2 W. That would cut a 10–20 W router on AC but leave it running on the 12 V car port. I could not open a Jackery page to confirm these figures.
standout_why: I compared against outagemath.com (cited), wattpowerstation.com/guides/portable-power-station-small-loads (cited), powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-standby-draw (cited in pm015) and our own page. Outagemath gives no timers, thresholds or per-model idle draw. Wattpowerstation already has Hobotech's DELTA Pro 3 figures (about 49 W with AC on, about 13 W with DC only), so the basic point that DC wastes less than AC is already out there. Powerstations.reviews lists DC-ECO timers for the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 and 200 V2 and 0.01 W no-load for the EcoFlow TRAIL DC units, but gives no load thresholds for any port. Our page says the Jackery 240 v2 mode shuts outputs after 12 h but gives no threshold. The threshold finding would be new and would decide the pick, which is why it would score 2–3. I could not open it on a Jackery page (jackery.com returned HTTP 429, the notice-facile manual copy returned 403, the otto.de manual PDF was too large), so the score stays at 1.
decides: It confirms the DC-port route. On stations whose default auto-off uses a high AC threshold and a very low DC threshold, a 10–20 W router stays up on the 12 V or USB-C port but gets switched off on AC unless the shopper disables the mode. On BLUETTI Elite V2 units with DC-ECO on by default, the shopper has to turn DC-ECO off first. For the 'least loss on USB/12 V' question, DC-only units with no inverter (EcoFlow TRAIL 300 DC, rated 0.01 W no-load) beat stations that run their DC side through a control board that stays on (Elite 30 V2: about 7–11 W with DC on, as measured by reviewers our page cites).

findings.source_title: Dealectric: Which small power station keeps a Wi-Fi router and modem running in a power outage (2026)
findings.note: Our own page, quoting the manual. It leaves out the watt thresholds, which are the part that matters for this angle.
